Los temas anteriores de este bloque dice: The previous topics in this block say what is covered and what gets failed. The mock paper brings the two together with a clock in front: questions from the topics of your subject, spread out as in the real paper, and a marking that says what to revise.
Un simulacro es un examen de verdad hech: A mock paper is a real exam taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. Here the questions come from the exercises of the Matemáticas II topics, spread across blocks as in the entrance paper, and each time you start one the numbers are different. On submitting, everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens and the score is computed block by block, with links to what is worth revising.
Discutir un sistema con un parámetro y r: Discussing a system with a parameter and solving it in some case; matrix equations, the inverse and powers of a matrix; properties of determinants.
Posición relativa de rectas y planos; ha: Relative position of lines and planes; finding a line or a plane satisfying given conditions; distances, angles, projections and reflected points.
Continuidad y derivabilidad con parámetr: Continuity and differentiability with parameters; limits and indeterminate forms; Bolzano's theorem and the mean value theorem; studying a function and optimisation; areas with integrals.
Probabilidad total y teorema de Bayes co: Total probability and Bayes' theorem with a tree or a table; the binomial distribution; the normal distribution and standardising.
El reparto de preguntas y minutos de est: The division of questions and minutes in this mock paper is indicative: each autonomous community decides how many questions it sets from each block and how many may be chosen. If your exam is different, untick the blocks you are not interested in and adjust the pace with the clock.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
<strong>Ten papel al lado y escribe el d: Keep paper beside you and write out the full working, as in the exam. Here only the result is checked; in the real paper, the setting-up and the steps are most of the marks, and an arithmetic slip with good method costs little.
<strong>Lee todas las preguntas antes de: Read all the questions before starting and begin with the ones you know best: it banks marks and calms the nerves.
<strong>Vigila el reloj por bloques.</st: Watch the clock block by block. If a part takes longer than its share, leave it and come back at the end. One blank part costs less than two questions left unattempted.
<strong>Comprueba antes de entregar</str: Check before submitting: substitute the solution of the system, see that an area is positive, that a probability lies between 0 and 1, that a point really is on the plane.
<strong>Lo importante no es la nota, sin: What matters is not the score but the final table. Each “To revise” link leads to the exact exercise that failed, and what you get wrong will come up again on the home page a few days later.
Llevas quince minutos en un apartado al: You have spent fifteen minutes on a part allotted ten and it will not come out. What do you do?
Seguir hasta que salga: ya casi está: Keep going until it comes out: you are almost there
«Ya casi está» es lo que se piensa siemp: “Almost there” is what you always think. Every extra minute here is a minute less for a question you do know.
Dejar escrito lo que hay, pasar al sigui: Leave what you have written, move on to the next and come back at the end
El planteamiento escrito ya puntúa. Con: The written setting-up already scores. With your head on another problem, on coming back you usually see the slip; and if not, the marks for the rest have been banked.
Tacharlo todo y empezar otro bloque: Cross it all out and start another block
Tachar borra lo que valía. Un planteamie: Crossing out deletes what was worth something. A correct unfinished setting-up is worth more than a blank page.
Discutir el sistema solo en los valores: Discussing the system only at the values that make the determinant vanish
El caso general, «$m$ distinto de esos v: The general case, “$m$ other than those values”, has to be written down too: it is consistent and determinate, and without saying so the discussion is incomplete.
El teorema exige función continua en un: The theorem demands a continuous function on a closed interval and different signs at the endpoints. Without the hypotheses written down, the justification does not count.
Dar la distancia a un plano sin dividir: Giving the distance to a plane without dividing by the magnitude of the normal
Sustituir el punto en la ecuación solo d: Substituting the point into the equation only gives the distance if the normal is a unit vector. It almost never is.
Señal segura de que faltó partir en los: A sure sign that splitting at the crossings with the axis was missed. An area is always positive; if it comes out negative, do not hand it in: check it.
El enlace de un simulacro corregido repr: The link of a marked mock paper reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and be able to compare results and methods.
Los exámenes de acceso a la universidad: University entrance exams in Spain are nearly a century old and have had many names. Selectividad, under that name, was brought in in 1974; in 2010 it became PAU, then EBAU or EvAU depending on the region, and since 2025 it is called PAU again, with papers that ask for more reasoning and applying and less repeating of procedures. What has not changed is what is assessed in mathematics: setting up well, computing carefully and explaining what you do.
